Manual CLI smoke-testing is blocked in this sandbox (no approval surface), but `npm test` passes with 9/9 tests including new coverage for `resolveDate`, and the existing `done()` test already exercises the date-marking path that the CLI now feeds into.

`habit done <name> [yesterday|today|YYYY-MM-DD]` now works — the CLI checks if the trailing arg parses as a date/keyword and, if so, splits it off before calling `done()`; otherwise the whole thing is treated as the habit name as before (so multi-word names are unaffected). Unparseable dates (bad format, invalid day/month) fall back to treating the full string as the name rather than erroring. Added `resolveDate` to `streak.js` and tests for it; `npm test` passes (9/9).

Options if you want to refine behavior: (1) make an invalid-looking date (e.g. `2026-13-40`) return an error instead of silently becoming part of the name, or (2) support future dates explicitly disallowed/allowed — currently any valid date, past or future, is accepted.
